caption: Frame: a titled box round the nodes that make the motion - the graph tidied, the effect unchanged
why: A graph of twenty nodes is hard to read when it is just nodes: which ones make the colour, which the motion, which the audio? Frame is a titled, coloured box you draw round a group of nodes - drag it and the nodes inside move with it.

Its neighbours: Note is text on the graph; sub-graphs (Node > Fold into a sub-graph) turn a group into a single node; Frame keeps the nodes visible but grouped. It changes nothing on the LEDs - the picture is the graph's own; the node is for whoever reads the graph.
steps: **title** is Motion: the words on the box's top edge.
**width** and **height** are its size in the graph (here 520 by 240), and **colour** its tint.
Inside it sit the **Time**, the **Multiply** and the **Wave** - the part of this graph that moves; the **Palette** and **Output** sit outside.
In the editor: drag the frame's title and the three nodes come along; select a few nodes and Node > Frame the selection draws one round them.
